page: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-64 is a general-purpose server instance powered by an Intel x86_64 processor. It features 64 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 256 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware.

The underlying Intel architecture supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE, AMX_INT8) and Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512, AVX_VNNI, AVX512_BF16). These hardware capabilities translate to strong performance in specialized compute tasks. Benchmarks show top-tier results in Passmark CPU extended instructions, encryption, and physics tests. Multi-core performance is highly competitive, as evidenced by strong Geekbench multi-core and software compilation scores.

The instance demonstrates high memory bandwidth, with read-only cached small block transfers reaching 4103.87 GB/sec and uncached large block transfers at 277.75 GB/sec. This memory efficiency supports demanding database operations and high-throughput web serving, with static web serving throughput measured at 86.82 GB/sec and Redis SET operations exceeding 70 million operations per second. Additionally, the AMX instructions facilitate efficient on-CPU LLM inference, processing 229.23 tokens per second for medium 7B model prompts.

Given its balanced resource allocation and lack of bundled local storage or GPUs, the n4-standard-64 offers a cost-efficient profile for scale-out enterprise workloads that require high memory bandwidth and multi-threaded CPU performance without the overhead of specialized accelerator hardware. It is highly suited for database hosting, software compilation pipelines, web serving at scale, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
description: The Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-64 is an x86_64 general-purpose server instance configured with 64 dedicated vCPUs (32 physical cores) and 256 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel processor with a 260 MB L3 cache, it supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX for matrix mathematics. The instance lacks local storage and GPUs but delivers strong performance across memory bandwidth and multi-core benchmarks. It achieves high throughput in database operations, software compilation, and static web serving, alongside efficient CPU-based LLM prompt processing. This resource profile makes the n4-standard-64 a highly capable option for enterprise applications, database hosting, and multi-threaded compute workloads.
